subject: Negative chi square values in DIF testing

messages.author: 6a96270785c153ae
messages.subject: Negative chi square values in DIF testing
parts:
Hi Phil,

I ran into some funky results in testing a measure for DIF where some of the DIF tests had negative chi-square values. My syntax is 

MvW_Wfreed = multipleGroup(MRNI_MvW_items, model, group = groups,
                               invariance = c('slopes', 'intercepts', 'free_means', 'free_var'),
                               technical = list(NCYCLES=5000))

MvW_DIFtest = DIF(MvW_Wfreed, c('a1', 'd1', 'd2', 'd3', 'd4', 'd5', 'd6'), scheme = 'drop', technical = list(NCYCLES=5000))

Most of the results look fine, but some came out like this:

$M21
       AIC        AICc        SABIC       HQ           BIC       logLik         X2        df     p
1 346235.6 346242.7 346769.5 346584.3 347243 -172968.8     NaN    NaN  NaN
2 346272.3 346280.1 346831.3 346637.4 347327 -172980.1    -22.722   7     1

Prior SEM tests of invariance indicated that metric invariance failed for all items in my comparison group, so I have a feeling that this could be the cause of the strange results. Still, I wanted to double check before I moved on.

Thanks,
Daniel

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Negative chi square values in DIF testing
parts:
My only guess here is as you imply; lack of convergence/termination issues (which can be more likely for graded response models) or a local minimum issue. For the clearly problematic items, you may have better luck explicitly fitting these nested models yourself to see if the problem can be isolated. That all said, if you can provide a simple reproducible example of this then I can try to see if the DIF() function can be made more robust to avoid issues like this in the future better. 

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Negative chi square values in DIF testing
parts:
Patch for this issue has been added. This was mainly due to non-convergence of the submodels, which in hindsight could have been avoided by using a better optimizer by default (such as the nlminb optimizer, which is slower but more robust). This is now the default in DIF(), and the starting values are selected based on the initial nested model. Feel free to download for the fix.

Phil
